mechanism_narrative: The continued decline in WORKPLACES mobility alongside only a mild recovery in TRANSIT and RETAIL_REC implies a still-weak commuting base. If that pattern persists, fewer weekday trips will convert into discretionary shopping visits, so retail-and-recreation mobility stays below its prior 4-week average over the next month.
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES rises for two consecutive weeks and RETAIL_REC is still lower over the next 28 days than over the last 28 days, the commuting-to-retail contraction mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL mobility falls while GROCERY_PHARM remains elevated, people are spending more time out of home for necessities rather than for discretionary outings. That substitution should lift RETAIL_REC within one week only if the extra out-of-home activity spills into shopping trips; otherwise retail mobility will not improve.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 4 points while GROCERY_PHARM stays above 8 points
failure_condition: If the trigger condition holds for a week but RETAIL_REC does not rise in the following week relative to the prior week, the spillover-to-shopping hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rebound in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES indicates loosened movement constraints and more cross-district circulation. That broader access should feed retail visitation with a two-week lag, producing higher RETAIL_REC versus the last four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT improves by at least 3 points week-on-week for two straight weeks
failure_condition: If TRANSIT improves for two weeks but RETAIL_REC remains flat or declines over the subsequent two weeks, the access-expansion mechanism fails.

mechanism_narrative: The recent rise in PARKS mobility suggests a leisure-weather or weekend-outing effect that can redirect trips away from indoor retail venues. If PARKS stays above its recent level, RETAIL_REC should weaken over the next four weeks as nonessential outings substitute toward outdoor space.
failure_condition: If PARKS remains elevated but RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days relative to the last 28 days, the outdoor-substitution mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Retail mobility should strengthen only when both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES recover together, because commuting provides the footfall that converts into shopping visits. A rise in one without the other will not be enough to lift RETAIL_REC, but a joint increase should do so within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both rise week-on-week
failure_condition: If both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES rise in the same week and RETAIL_REC does not increase within the next two weeks, the commuting-synergy hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: Elevated GROCERY_PHARM combined with rising RESIDENTIAL mobility signals more time spent near home and fewer long discretionary trips. That home-centered routine should suppress retail-and-recreation visits over the next month, keeping RETAIL_REC below its recent average.
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM stays high and RESIDENTIAL remains above its recent level but RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days, the home-centered suppression mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in TRANSIT below its recent range is a direct signal of mobility friction or service disruption. If that threshold is crossed, discretionary retail trips should fall within one week because fewer riders can reach shopping corridors easily.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -18 points and stays there for one weekly mean
failure_condition: If TRANSIT drops below -18 but RETAIL_REC does not decline in the following week, the disruption-threshold hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: During a recovery phase, rising PARKS mobility paired with falling RESIDENTIAL mobility marks a substitution from staying home to taking trips outside the home. In that regime, retail activity should rise over the next two weeks because the same households are already more willing to travel.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises while RESIDENTIAL falls in the same week
failure_condition: If PARKS rises and RESIDENTIAL falls together but RETAIL_REC fails to increase over the next two weeks, the outdoor-discretionary conversion mechanism fails.
